questions.question: Which of the following options represents the correct mirror image of the given figure?

options.explanation: This option is incorrect because the base is not symmetrical.
This option is incorrect because the letter 'R' is not mirrored.
This option is correct because the letter 'R' is mirrored to 'Я' and the symmetrical base remains unchanged.
This option is incorrect because the base is not symmetrical.

questions.explanation: In a mirror image, the left and right sides of an object are interchanged, while the top and bottom remain the same. The letter 'R' becomes 'Я'. The triangular base structure is symmetrical and remains unchanged in its overall shape, but its internal lines would also flip if they were asymmetrical. In this case, the symmetrical base remains visually the same.

questions.question: What is the correct mirror image of the time "4:30" shown on a clock face?

options.explanation: This option is incorrect because it is not the correct mirror image.
This option is incorrect because it is not the correct mirror image.
This option is correct because it is the correct mirror image of the time 4:30.
This option is incorrect because it is not the correct mirror image.

questions.explanation: To find the mirror image of a clock time, subtract the given time from 11:60. 11:60 - 4:30 = 7:30. Alternatively, visualize the clock. At 4:30, the hour hand is between 4 and 5, and the minute hand is at 6. In the mirror image, the minute hand at 6 remains at 6. The hour hand, which was 4.5 hours past 12, will now be 4.5 hours before 12, which is 7.5. So, the hour hand will be between 7 and 8. The time displayed would be 7:30.

questions.question: Select the correct mirror image of the following figure when the mirror is placed below the figure. The figure is a large capital letter 'M'. Inside the left diagonal stroke, there is a small upward-pointing triangle. Inside the right diagonal stroke, there is a small downward-pointing arrow.

options.text: A large 'M'. Triangle upward in the left stroke. Arrow downward in the right stroke.
options.explanation: This option does not describe the correct vertical inversion of the figure.

options.text: A large 'W'. Triangle downward in the left stroke. Arrow upward in the right stroke.
options.explanation: This option correctly describes the vertical inversion of the figure.

options.text: A large 'W'. Triangle upward in the left stroke. Arrow downward in the right stroke.
options.explanation: This option does not correctly describe the inversion of the triangle and the arrow.

options.text: A large 'W'. Triangle downward in the left stroke. Arrow upward in the right stroke.
options.explanation: This option is a duplicate of option B and is not a valid alternative.

questions.explanation: When the mirror is placed below the figure, it undergoes vertical inversion (upside down), while left-right orientation remains the same. The capital 'M' will invert vertically to become 'W'. The small upward-pointing triangle in the left diagonal stroke will invert vertically to become a downward-pointing triangle, still in the left diagonal stroke (of the 'W'). The small downward-pointing arrow in the right diagonal stroke will invert vertically to become an upward-pointing arrow, still in the right diagonal stroke (of the 'W').
questions.subject: chsl-reasoning

questions.explanation: Each character is laterally inverted, and the sequence is reversed. 'B' becomes 'Я', '@' remains '@' (it's symmetrical or its inversion looks very similar in most fonts), '1' remains '1', 'S' becomes 'S', and 'T' remains 'T'. So, 'B@1ST' becomes 'TⱢ@Я'.
